I farm the way I have learned over many years in Quzhou: I keep the full 10.1 mu in the wheat-maize rotation because that matches my land, my irrigation conditions, and the labor my family can still organize. I will plant winter wheat on all 10.1 mu, then follow it with summer maize on the same 10.1 mu after wheat harvest. Since I have well irrigation, I will rely on stable water at the key stages instead of gambling on rainfall. I do not want risky low-input management, but I also will not push inputs too hard because fertilizer and pesticide cost money and I care about steady output more than chasing the highest possible yield. For wheat, I will use improved seed, enough nitrogen to support tillering and grain filling, moderate phosphorus for rooting, some potassium for plant strength, and several irrigations because wheat here responds well to water. I will use rotary tillage because it is practical and fits the rotation. For maize, I will use hybrid seed because that is what gives me the most reliable yield on this kind of land. I will apply moderate-to-high nitrogen, balanced phosphorus and potassium, irrigate at the main growth stages, and keep pesticide use limited to what is needed for weeds and common pests. With my experience and the conditions I have, this is the plan I will follow to keep yields stable and the work manageable.
